title: The Gallic War (Commentarii de Bello Gallico)
author: Julius Caesar
blurb: Caesar's own dispatches from Gaul, written in the third person. Spin and clarity in equal measure — still the first Latin text most students read.

title: History of Rome (Ab Urbe Condita)
author: Livy
blurb: 142 books from the founding to 9 BC, of which 35 survive. The Republic's official memory, with a moral in every chapter.

title: The Histories
author: Polybius
blurb: A Greek hostage explains how Rome conquered the Mediterranean in 53 years — and why its mixed constitution worked.

title: The Annals and The Histories
author: Tacitus
blurb: Tiberius to Nero, then the Year of the Four Emperors, by the sharpest stylist in Latin. Sine ira et studio — allegedly.

title: The Twelve Caesars
author: Suetonius
blurb: Gossip, omens and administration for Julius Caesar through Domitian. Where most of the best stories come from.

title: Parallel Lives
author: Plutarch
blurb: Greek and Roman lives in pairs: Caesar, Antony, Cicero, the Gracchi. Shakespeare's source, and everybody else's.

title: Roman History
author: Cassius Dio
blurb: Eighty books from Aeneas to 229; the main narrative for the Augustan settlement and the Severans.

title: Res Gestae Divi Augusti
author: Augustus
blurb: The emperor's own CV, inscribed in bronze outside his mausoleum and copied onto temples across the Empire. Humble it is not.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
blurb: Private notes to himself, in Greek, from the Danube front. The most-read Stoic text and a decent operating manual for emperors.

title: The Later Roman Empire (Res Gestae)
author: Ammianus Marcellinus
blurb: A soldier's history of 353–378, ending at Adrianople. The last great Latin historian.

title: The Jewish War
author: Josephus
blurb: An eyewitness account of the revolt of 66–73, the siege of Jerusalem and Masada, by a commander who changed sides.

title: Satires
author: Juvenal
blurb: Bread and circuses, who guards the guards, and a great deal of complaining about Rome. Still accurate about cities.

title: Letters
author: Pliny the Younger
blurb: Vesuvius from across the bay, the Christians of Bithynia, and what a Roman senator thought about on a Tuesday.

title: The Aeneid
author: Virgil
blurb: Rome's founding epic — Troy to Italy — commissioned under Augustus. Imperium sine fine.

title: The Secret History
author: Procopius
blurb: Justinian's court historian, unfiltered: Theodora, Belisarius, and an emperor who may literally be a demon.

title: De Re Militari
author: Vegetius
blurb: How the legions were supposed to work, written when they no longer did. Required reading for medieval generals.

title: The Satyricon
author: Petronius
blurb: Trimalchio's dinner party: new money, bad taste, great comedy, from Nero's arbiter of elegance.

title: De Architectura
author: Vitruvius
blurb: Firmitas, utilitas, venustas. The only surviving architecture treatise from antiquity; it explains the concrete.

title: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
author: Edward Gibbon
blurb: Six volumes, one immortal prose style, and the thesis everyone has argued with since. Start with the footnotes.

title: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome
author: Mary Beard
blurb: From the founding myths to Caracalla's citizenship edict, with a constant eye on what the evidence actually is.

title: Emperor of Rome: Ruling the Ancient Roman World
author: Mary Beard
blurb: Not a parade of emperors but a job description: what it was like to be one, serve one, and survive one.

title: Rubicon: The Triumph and Tragedy of the Roman Republic
author: Tom Holland
blurb: The last century of the Republic as political thriller: Sulla, Pompey, Caesar, Octavian.

title: Dynasty: The Rise and Fall of the House of Caesar
author: Tom Holland
blurb: The Julio-Claudians from Augustus to Nero. Family drama at imperial scale.

title: Caesar: Life of a Colossus
author: Adrian Goldsworthy
blurb: The standard modern biography, with a soldier's eye for the campaigns.

title: Augustus: First Emperor of Rome
author: Adrian Goldsworthy
blurb: How a sickly teenager became the most successful politician in history and made it look like a restoration.

title: Pax Romana: War, Peace and Conquest in the Roman World
author: Adrian Goldsworthy
blurb: What the "Roman peace" actually meant for the people living under it.

title: The Roman Revolution
author: Ronald Syme
blurb: Augustus as the leader of a faction, not the saviour of the state. Cold, brilliant, and written as Europe's dictators rose.

title: Mortal Republic: How Rome Fell into Tyranny
author: Edward J. Watts
blurb: How norms eroded one exception at a time until Augustus. Written with one eye on the present.

title: The Storm Before the Storm
author: Mike Duncan
blurb: 146–78 BC: the Gracchi, Marius and Sulla, by the History of Rome podcaster. How the Republic learned to break its own rules.

title: The Fall of the Roman Empire: A New History of Rome and the Barbarians
author: Peter Heather
blurb: The Huns pushed, the Goths moved, the West broke. A forceful case that the barbarians really did do it.

title: The Fall of Rome and the End of Civilization
author: Bryan Ward-Perkins
blurb: Archaeology says the fall was real: roof tiles, pottery, cattle size. Short, sharp and unromantic.

title: The Fate of Rome: Climate, Disease, and the End of an Empire
author: Kyle Harper
blurb: Volcanoes, plague and a cooling climate as co-conspirators in the fall. The environmental history.

title: The Inheritance of Rome: A History of Europe from 400 to 1000
author: Chris Wickham
blurb: What happened to the Roman world after it stopped being the Roman world.

title: Byzantium: The Early Centuries · The Apogee · The Decline and Fall
author: John Julius Norwich
blurb: The readable narrative of the other thousand years of Roman history. Also condensed as A Short History of Byzantium.

title: The Grand Strategy of the Roman Empire
author: Edward N. Luttwak
blurb: The frontier system analysed as strategy. Contested by historians, loved by generals.

title: Justinian's Flea
author: William Rosen
blurb: The Plague of Justinian and the end of the ancient world's last reconquest.

title: Ancient Rome: The Rise and Fall of an Empire
author: Simon Baker
blurb: The BBC companion volume: six pivotal moments told as narrative. The easy on-ramp.

title: I, Claudius
author: Robert Graves
blurb: The Julio-Claudians as family tragedy, narrated by the stammering survivor. Sequel: Claudius the God.

title: Memoirs of Hadrian
author: Marguerite Yourcenar
blurb: The emperor's long letter to the young Marcus Aurelius. Possibly the best novel ever written about power and mortality.

title: Masters of Rome (series)
author: Colleen McCullough
blurb: Seven novels from Marius to Octavian, researched down to the sestertius.

title: Imperium (Cicero trilogy)
author: Robert Harris
blurb: Cicero's career, told by his secretary Tiro — inventor of shorthand. A political thriller in a toga.

title: Pompeii
author: Robert Harris
blurb: An aqueduct engineer notices the water has stopped. Two days before 24 August 79.

title: Julian
author: Gore Vidal
blurb: The Apostate's memoir, annotated by two bickering philosophers.

title: The Eagle of the Ninth
author: Rosemary Sutcliff
blurb: A lost legion, the Romano-British frontier, and the book that made a generation of historians.

title: Quo Vadis
author: Henryk Sienkiewicz
blurb: Nero's Rome, the early Christians, and a Nobel Prize.

title: Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ
author: Lew Wallace
blurb: Galleys, the chariot race, revenge. The bestselling American novel of the nineteenth century.
